---
title: "sub() silently turns its input into text"
ref: FCT-06
categories: [Factors]
impact: incoherent
extrait: 'sub("T", "", T)'
reponse: '"RUE"'
attendu: "an error, `T` is not text"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sub("T", "", T)
sub("0", "", 100000)
sub("_.*", "", factor(c("a_1", "b_2")))
```
:::

## Why

`sub()` and `gsub()` first apply `as.character()` to whatever they are given, without warning. `TRUE` becomes `"TRUE"`, and the replacement works on that text.

For a number, the spelling R picks is what counts: `100000` is written `"1e+05"`, so removing the first zero gives `"1e+5"`. A factor, for its part, comes out as a character vector.

## The fix

Convert to text yourself, in the format you want, before doing a replacement.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
sub("0", "", format(100000, scientific = FALSE))
x <- factor(c("a_1", "b_2"))
levels(x) <- sub("_.*", "", levels(x))
x
```
:::
